cli.help:
Cairn — storage analysis, backups and git maintenance for your Mac.

Usage: cairn <command> [options]

Commands:
  analyze [folder…]   Analyze disk usage of folders
  ai                  List AI tools and what is backed up
  backup [--dry-run]  Back up to the configured destinations
  verify [--full]     Check backup integrity
  restore [--apply]   Restore a backup (simulation by default)
  git [--apply]       Clean up gone branches and stale worktrees
  tools [--export D]  List CLI tools to reinstall
  config <cmd>        Show or validate the configuration (path, show, validate)
  version             Show the Cairn version
  help                Show this help

Options:
  --config <file>       Use another configuration file
  --lang <en-US|fr-FR>  Language for this run
  -h, --help            Show help

cli.git.help:
Usage: cairn git [options]

Finds local branches whose remote branch was deleted ("gone") and stale worktrees, then optimizes repositories.
SIMULATION by default: nothing changes without --apply.

  --root DIR           Folder to scan (default: tracked folders)
  --only PATTERN       Only repositories whose path contains PATTERN
  --fetch              git fetch --prune first (network)
  --apply              Delete selected branches and worktrees, then git gc
  --yes                Do not ask for confirmation
  --include-unmerged   With --apply: also delete unmerged gone branches
  --prune-now          With --apply: free space now (deleted branches can no longer be recovered)
  --no-gc              Do not run git gc
  --worktrees-only     Only worktrees
  --stale-days N       Worktree inactive after N days
  --include-at-risk    Also remove worktrees with uncommitted or unpushed work
  --report FILE        Write the TSV report
  --json               Machine-readable output

Usage: cairn verify [--destination ID] [--version V] [--full]

Checks backup integrity with the SHA-256 checksums of each version: a sample of the latest version by default, every file of every version with --full. Exit code 1 if a damaged file is found.
